evals.prompt: Build a retro analog synth panel in React: oscillator waveform, a filter with cutoff and resonance, an amp envelope and a master volume with a stereo meter. It must look like real vintage hardware. The project has no shadcn and no Tailwind.
evals.expected_output: @audio-ui/react primitives styled from styles/base.css and styles/retro.css with hardware taste: sections by signal flow, a larger master knob, printed labels, one amber lamp.
expectations: Reads the skill's design.md and directions.md, and states the chosen direction in one sentence before writing CSS

Imports only primitives that exist from @audio-ui/react (or @audio-ui/react/<entry>), with the real part tree: Knob.Root > Control > Track/Indicator/Thumb, Meter.Channels given a render function, Fader.Control containing Track and Thumb
Gives the parts the structure of styles/base.css (a sized control, a sized fader track, a flex Meter.Root with a height) and never sets position, bottom, left, translate or rotate on a thumb
Every control has an aria-label or a Label part, and a :focus-visible style exists
Uses the retro skin (skin-retro class and styles/retro.css) and does not add gradients, glass or glow from another direction
Groups the controls in labelled sections that follow the signal (oscillator, filter, amplifier, output), not one grid of equal knobs
The master volume is larger than the other knobs, and no more than three knob sizes are used
Labels are small uppercase tracked text and values use tabular numbers
Glow appears only on lamps (a power or clip lamp), not on knobs or the panel
The meter's zones are painted at the full channel size (background-size equal to the channel height), not on the shrinking indicator

evals.prompt: Make a minimalist mixer with four channel strips: a fader, a mute and a stereo meter for each, plus a master. Clean, quiet, editorial. Plain CSS, no component library.
evals.expected_output: Four faders and meters on the minimal skin: paper background, hairlines, one accent, generous spacing.
expectations: Reads the skill's design.md and directions.md, and states the chosen direction in one sentence before writing CSS

Gives the parts the structure of styles/base.css (a sized control, a sized fader track, a flex Meter.Root with a height) and never sets position, bottom, left, translate or rotate on a thumb
Every control has an aria-label or a Label part, and a :focus-visible style exists
Uses the minimal skin: no shadows, no gradients, radius of 2px or less, one accent color
Uses one accent color for value and the active state, and a second hue only for clipping

evals.prompt: Design a modern dark equalizer plugin UI: four band knobs, a gain fader, an input meter and an output meter. It should feel like a professional tool, nothing like a landing page.
evals.expected_output: The modern skin: flat graphite surfaces, hairline borders, one signal color, mono labels, no glow or purple gradients.
expectations: Reads the skill's design.md and directions.md, and states the chosen direction in one sentence before writing CSS

evals.prompt: I use Tailwind and shadcn/ui. Add a drum machine page with eight pads and a tempo knob, and give it a skeuomorphic hardware look.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the registry components where the project has shadcn, picks the retro direction for the look and applies the design rules to the panel.
expectations: States the direction (retro hardware) in one sentence before styling
Uses semantic tokens or the retro skin's own scoped variables, and does not mix a second direction into the panel
Pad strikes are drawn from data-active and the --pad-velocity variable, and sink physically (a short translate and a shorter shadow)
Decorative pieces such as screws and lamps have aria-hidden and pointer-events none

evals.prompt: Make a modular-synth style panel in React with six small knobs, a patch of four sliders and a stereo meter. It should look like a black Eurorack-like panel with thin white print and one red accent. No shadcn.
evals.expected_output: A new direction composed from styles/materials.css: tokens plus a material per part, not one of the shipped skins copied.
expectations: Reads taste.md and states the direction as decisions (surface, light, materials, color, type, shape) before writing CSS
Copies styles/base.css and styles/materials.css and defines its own scope class with the tokens (panel, ink, accent, hi, lo), instead of editing retro.css or modern.css
Picks a material per part from the vocabulary (plastic, brushed, groove, zones, segments) with background: var(--...) and the shared shadows
Uses one accent (the red) and no purple or cyan gradients, no glow on knobs, no glass
Uses the verified part tree and the kit's class names, so every part has a size, and keeps focus rings, labels and hit areas
Draws decorative pieces (jacks, screws) with aria-hidden and pointer-events none
